title: Insomnia Disorder - Criteria
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Criteria

CORE ALIASES: Chronic insomnia, insomnia disorder, sleep onset/maintenance insomnia.

DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA:
A. A predominant complaint of dissatisfaction with sleep quantity or quality, associated with one (or more) of the following:
1. Difficulty initiating sleep
2. Difficulty maintaining sleep, with frequent awakenings or problems returning to sleep after awakenings
3. Early-morning awakening with inability to return to sleep
B. The sleep disturbance causes clinically significant distress or impairment.
C. The sleep difficulty occurs at least 3 nights per week.
D. The sleep difficulty has been present for at least 3 months.
E. The sleep difficulty occurs despite adequate opportunity for sleep.
F. Not better explained by another sleep-wake disorder, substance, or medical condition.

REQUIRED FEATURES: Dissatisfaction with sleep + difficulty initiating/maintaining/early awakening + 3 nights/week + 3 months + distress/impairment.

RULE-OUTS / DIFFERENTIALS: Sleep Apnea, Restless Legs, Circadian Rhythm Disorders, Substance-induced, Medical (hyperthyroidism, pain), Psychiatric (MDD, GAD, PTSD with sleep symptoms).

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: "I sleep fine once I get to sleep", "only when stressed but resolves quickly", "daytime sleepiness is the main problem".

PROVENANCE: DSM-5-TR. AASM and APA guidelines recommend CBT-I as first-line.
